hooks.text: NASA intentionally crashed a three-billion-dollar spacecraft into Saturn's crushing atmosphere.
Why did NASA deliberately murder its most successful three-billion-dollar probe?
NASA vaporized a three-billion-dollar spacecraft to protect life it hasn't found.

title: Why NASA Killed a $3B Spacecraft
description: NASA intentionally crashed the Cassini spacecraft into Saturn's atmosphere to protect its moons from Earthly bacteria.

beats.text: NASA intentionally crashed a three-billion-dollar spacecraft into Saturn's crushing atmosphere.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of Cassini orbiting Saturn, 2017

beats.text: The Cassini-Huygens mission, a joint international effort, arrived at the ringed planet in July 2004.
beats.visual: Cassini spacecraft arriving at Saturn illustration, 2004

beats.text: The spacecraft discovered geysers of water ice on Enceladus and methane seas on the massive moon Titan.
beats.visual: Plumes of water ice erupting from Enceladus captured by Cassini, 2005

beats.text: These worlds had everything needed for life, but Cassini was running out of rocket fuel.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of Cassini near Saturn's rings, 2017

beats.text: Scientists realized if the dead probe ever drifted and crashed, Earthly microbes could contaminate these pristine moons.
beats.visual: NASA technician in a clean room with spacecraft components

beats.text: To prevent a biological disaster, they ordered a 'Grand Finale' dive through the rings and into Saturn's clouds.
beats.visual: Diagram of Cassini's Grand Finale orbits between Saturn and its rings

beats.text: On September 15, 2017, Cassini fought Saturn's winds for 30 seconds longer than predicted before burning up.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of Cassini burning up in Saturn's atmosphere, 2017

beats.text: This was a calculated sacrifice to protect moons that might hold life from the three-billion-dollar spacecraft.
beats.visual: Cassini mission team at JPL reacting to final signal loss, 2017

better_than_last: Used a mystery structure to escalate the stakes of microbial contamination before revealing the Grand Finale plunge.
